dose_child: Indications: High fever (>38.5 °C) or ear pain. Schedule: For ear pain: Give one dose every 6 hours or until the ear pain is gone. Give mother enough for 1 day (4 doses).

Indications: Pneumonia, Acute Ear Infection, Dysentery. Schedule: 2-12 months: Pediatric tablet (20mg trimethoprim/100mg sulphamethoxazole): 2 tablets twice daily for 5 days. Syrup: 5 ml twice daily. 12m-5y: Pediatric tablet: 3 tablets twice daily for 5 days. Syrup: 7.5 ml twice daily.
dose_adult: 800 mg SMX / 160 mg TMP (1 double strength tablet) twice daily
contraindications: Avoid in a young infant less than 1 month of age who is premature or jaundiced.
pregnancy_note: Avoid in first trimester (folate antagonist) and near term (risk of kernicterus).

dose_child: Indications: Pneumonia, Acute Ear Infection (Second-line). Schedule: 2-12 months: Syrup (125mg/5ml): 5 ml three times daily for 5 days. 12m-5y: Syrup (125mg/5ml): 10 ml three times daily for 5 days.

Indications: First-line oral antimalarial. Schedule: Give for 3 days. Dose is reduced on the third day unless child weighs <10kg and giving 150mg base tablets. Side effects: Itching is a possible side effect.
Indications: Measles or Severe Malnutrition. Schedule: Give 2 doses. First dose in clinic, second dose next day at home. Danger of overdose if repeated too frequently.
pregnancy_note: High doses are teratogenic; limit to 10k IU/day unless treating severe deficiency.

dose_child: Indications: Anaemia (some palmar pallor). Schedule: Give syrup to child <12 months. Give tablets if >=12 months. One dose daily for 14 days. Side effects: May make stools black. Overdose can be fatal.
dose_adult: 60 mg elemental iron (with folate) 1-2 times daily
contraindications: Do not give with sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine if iron syrup contains folate.

dose_child: Indications: Hookworm or whipworm infection contributing to anaemia in children >= 2 years. Schedule: 500 mg mebendazole as a single dose in clinic.
